title: Priyanka Chopra Jonas Returns to Indian Cinema as Mandakini in SS Rajamouli's Epic Varanasi
excerpt: Priyanka Chopra Jonas returns to Indian cinema in SS Rajamouli's Varanasi after a four-year hiatus.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Priyanka Chopra Jonas returns to Indian cinema in SS Rajamouli's Varanasi after a four-year hiatus.
  • Varanasi's production budget is estimated at Rs 1,300 crore ($150 million), making it one of India's costliest films.
  • The film features Mahesh Babu and Prithviraj Sukumaran, with music by Oscar-winner MM Keeravani.
  • Set for a 2027 release, Varanasi is Rajamouli's first original film since the success of RRR.
  • Entertainment Weekly has released exclusive new images of Priyanka Chopra Jonas as Mandakini in SS Rajamouli's upcoming epic Varanasi, marking her first Indian theatrical release since 2019's The Sky Is Pink.
  • Varanasi spans thousands of years across Antarctica, Africa, and India, with an estimated production budget of Rs 1,300 crore ($150 million), making it one of the most expensive Indian films ever.
  • The film stars Mahesh Babu as Rudhra and Prithviraj Sukumaran as the antagonist Kumbha, with music by Oscar-winner MM Keeravani.
  • Directed and written by the filmmaker behind RRR, Varanasi is set for a 2027 worldwide release in standard and IMAX theaters.
https://x.com/ssrajamouli/status/2078318224677179461

Priyanka Chopra Jonas is making her long-awaited return to Indian cinema. Entertainment Weekly has exclusively revealed new images of the actress in SS Rajamouli's Varanasi, where she plays Mandakini — described as "fierce, globetrotting" and "strong, vulnerable, and unforgettable in equal measure."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=XJgaqgZiLyY

It is Chopra Jonas's first Indian theatrical release since 2019's The Sky Is Pink, and arguably her most ambitious Indian project to date. The film reunites her with the director who turned RRR into a global phenomenon and won the Academy Award for Best Original Song with "Naatu Naatu."

![The Sky Is Pink — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/9/93/The_Sky_Is_Pink.jpg)

An Epic Scope

> **"Shruti Haasan performed the film's popular "Sanchaari" track on stage, composed by Oscar-winner MM Keeravani."**

Varanasi is described as an epic action-adventure that spans thousands of years, from ancient civilizations to the present day, across multiple continents. Characters traverse Antarctica, Africa, and the holy city of Varanasi itself — which Rajamouli recreated in Hyderabad, replicating its famous ghats, temples, and palatial architecture.

The film was shot across India, Kenya's Maasai Mara (with special government access to film alongside real wild animals), and other international locations. Its estimated production budget of Rs 1,300 crore (approximately $150 million), excluding marketing, makes it one of the most expensive Indian films ever produced.

Mahesh Babu stars as Rudhra, the male lead, who also plays Lord Rama in a secondary role. Prithviraj Sukumaran plays Kumbha, the primary antagonist — described as a man who uses a wheelchair and is "dangerously unlimited in his mentality." Chopra's Mandakini finds herself caught between both men.

![Mahesh Babu — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9a/Mahesh_Babu_in_Spyder_%28cropped%29.jpg)

A Homecoming for Chopra Jonas

The role marks a significant homecoming for Chopra Jonas, who has spent recent years building her Hollywood career with projects including Citadel and The Bluff. At the Varanasi launch event in Hyderabad last November, she was seen backstage rehearsing Telugu lines, approaching the moment with what Filmfare described as "meticulous care."

— Priyanka Chopra Jonas, sharing behind-the-scenes footage from the launch event

The launch event at Ramoji Film City drew 50,000 fans chanting for Mahesh Babu. Shruti Haasan performed the film's popular "Sanchaari" track on stage, composed by Oscar-winner MM Keeravani. Chopra Jonas praised co-star Sukumaran as "terrifying on screen but the opposite in real life" and hailed Rajamouli as the visionary who "brought Indian cinema to the world."

![Prithviraj Sukumaran — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/48/Prithviraj_at_Aiyyaa_event.jpg)

Rajamouli's First Original Since RRR

Varanasi is Rajamouli's first original film since RRR's global breakout. The project had been in development since discussions between Rajamouli and Mahesh Babu began in 2010, but materialized only after RRR's completion. The screenplay was developed by Rajamouli alongside V. Vijayendra Prasad, SS Kanchi, S. Gopal Reddy, and Deva Katta, with principal photography beginning in Hyderabad in February 2025.

The film draws comparisons to the Indiana Jones and James Bond franchises for its globe-trotting adventure structure. Its working title was "Globe Trotter" before the Varanasi reveal. It is being produced by Sri Durga Arts and Showing Business, and is set for a 2027 worldwide release in standard and IMAX theaters.

Why It Matters

For the Indian diaspora, Varanasi represents a convergence: a globally recognized Indian star returning to work with arguably Indian cinema's most internationally successful director, in a film scaled to compete with Hollywood tentpoles. Chopra Jonas's involvement bridges the Bollywood-Hollywood divide in a way few Indian actors have managed, while Rajamouli's track record suggests the film will aim for both Indian and international audiences.
